artworks.title: Athamas Killing Ino's Son
artworks.description: Gandolfi's oil shows the Boeotian king in the grip of Hera's madness: Athamas seizes the infant Learchus while Ino recoils with Melicertes — the Ovidian catastrophe that ends in the leap from the Molurian rock and the children's sea-change into Palaemon and Leucothea.

artworks.title: Athamas Tearing Apart His Children
artworks.description: A pen-and-wash design for Ovid's Metamorphoses: Athamas dashes Learchus against the palace while Ino flees with Melicertes and Tisiphone still haunts the stair — the Fury's visit made legible as domestic slaughter.

artworks.title: The Insane Athamas Killing Learchus, While Ino and Melicertes Jump into the Sea
artworks.description: Tempesta's engraving (published by Wilhelm Janson) freezes the double climax of the myth: Athamas murdering Learchus indoors as Ino and Melicertes leap toward the sea that will remake them as marine gods.

artworks.title: The Fury Tisiphone at the Palace of Athamas
artworks.description: The companion plate opens the same Ovidian sequence: Tisiphone enters Athamas' house with snakes and torch, sowing the madness that will turn the king against his own children.

artworks.title: Study for The Fury of Athamas
artworks.description: Flaxman's chalk study for his marble group (Ickworth) abstracts Athamas' frenzy into a neoclassical knot of bodies — the king, the murdered child, and Ino's flight distilled for sculpture.

popCulture.title: Golden Fleece
popCulture.description: Athamas' household is the fleece's origin: the golden ram that saved Phrixus from the king's madness still begins every Argonaut story.

popCulture.title: Athamas
popCulture.description: Athamas endures as the king Hera drove mad — the father who hunts his own children and seeds the voyage for the fleece.
